source.title: Learning From Noisy Labels via Dynamic Loss Thresholding
source.authors: Hao Yang; Youzhi Jin; Zi-Yi Li; Deng-Bao Wang; Lei Miao; Xin Geng; Min-Ling Zhang

record.tranche_reason: Tests how networks learn from partially corrupted image labels, using loss trajectories and test accuracy; it does not reproduce fully random-label training.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work for fitting noisy labels. Its own results include a cross-entropy loss trajectory and test accuracy under several label-noise conditions. The cited prior results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study's own standard cross-entropy loss trajectories test clean-before-noisy learning (V6), and its baseline test accuracies bear on the degradation component of V4. These results go beyond using memorization as a premise for DLT.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete: the authors propose DLT to distinguish clean and noisy samples using dynamic loss thresholds, discard suspect labels, and exploit those images through semi-supervised learning. They also report noise-rate estimation from early-to-late loss differences and successful handling of generated hard samples.
record.recipe_differences: Uses image classification with controlled label corruption and standard cross-entropy as a baseline, but focuses on noisy-label learning and DLT rather than training on completely random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise type and rate; CIFAR-10 versus CIFAR-100; the paper reports different test accuracy across these settings.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
record.problems: The relevant table reports test accuracy, not training error. No completely random-label condition is tested, and no uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No results beyond the six CIFAR-10 standard cross-entropy entries in Table 1 and the Figure 1(a) loss trajectory were included. Other methods' noisy-label results are not the claim's standard-training condition; CIFAR-100 and Clothing1M test-accuracy results were omitted because they likewise do not report training fit and do not add a distinct condition needed for V4.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged hyperparameters relative to true-label training.
Relative time required to fit true and random labels, and convergence-time changes across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit across corruption fractions; endpoints at no corruption and completely random labels; approach to chance over the full corruption range. The recorded table tests only intermediate-rate test-performance degradation.
Whether explicit regularization prevents fitting completely random labels, and whether removing regularization preserves true-label generalization.
Generality beyond the demonstrated partially corrupted CIFAR-10 setting, and direct identification of shared representations rather than inference from clean/noisy loss trajectories.

missing.what: The additional early-versus-late loss comparison reports separated clean/noisy losses early and similar losses late, corroborating differential learning over training. Exact loss values are not supplied in the text.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V4 limits_scope verdict: missing training-fit measurements are untested components, and above-chance accuracy at 60% corruption is compatible with V4. The supplied text explicitly connects the study's own Figure 1(a) to V6, so V6 is tested rather than merely cited. Other CIFAR-100 and method-performance results were explicitly declared omitted.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on completely random labels or report training error and test error at chance under that condition.
Does not compare training time to fit true versus random labels or report convergence time across corruption fractions.
Does not train on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Does not report training error across corruption fractions or show that training fit remains perfect; its test-accuracy table does not establish a steady rise to chance.
No comparison removes weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation to test fitting random labels or generalization on true labels.
The paper cites the prior pattern-learning result but does not test real versus random labels over training. Its own hard-sample analysis is not a test of this version.

rows.subject: 18-layer PreAct Resnet
rows.operation_detail: Standard cross-entropy training; per-sample losses for clean and noisy examples tracked over training.
rows.measure: Cross-entropy loss trajectory for clean and noisy samples; authors state that training with cross-entropy fits noisy labels.
rows.value: Figure shows loss trajectories; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The paper explicitly describes fitting noisy labels, but this does not establish zero training error or test error at chance.
rows.check: Figure 1(a) and the accompanying introduction explicitly report clean samples being fitted before noisy samples, with larger noisy-sample losses early in training. This directly tests V6. A single corruption-rate loss trajectory does not establish V4's across-rate relationship or perfect training accuracy.
